title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 63
paragraphs: Thus Ariston had brought into his house the third wife, having dismissed the second; and this wife, not having fulfilled the ten months but in a shorter period of time, bore him the Demaratus of whom we were speaking. One of his servants reported to him, as he was sitting in council with the Ephors, that a son had been born to him. He then, knowing the time when he had taken the wife, and reckoning the months on his fingers, said, denying with an oath: “The child would not be mine.” The Ephors heard this but thought it a matter of no importance at the time; and the child grew up, and Ariston repented of what he had said, for he thought Demaratus was certainly his own son. He gave him the name “Demaratus” for this reason: because before these events the Spartan people as a whole had made a vow, praying that a son might be born to Ariston as one who was preeminent in renown above all the kings who had ever arisen in Sparta.
